Short answers up front: yes, we can produce a compact latency matrix and two pilot packaging options by Friday. Recommended quant path: start with per-layer-aware int8 quant (via our Optimize toolkit profile) for encoder-decoder and int8/16 mixed for generative heads — this typically preserves >98% of human-eval parity for chat workloads we see in similar customers. Full details below.

Packaging options (sketch):
- Option A: Credit-based pilot — 100k token credit bundle + profiling support. No commit beyond credits. Good for small teams.
- Option B: Short-term commit — 6-week reserved slot (soft commit) with 10% pilot credit concession, includes 2 profiler sessions and latency matrix deliverable. Best when you want predictable throughput and a controlled discount.

Technical deliverables if you pick Option B (recommended):
- KV-cache vs no-cache latency matrix (p50/p95) across three seq lengths (64/256/512), batch sizes (1/4/8).
- Profiling session (30–45m) where we run a representative trace on your sample prompt set.
- Quantization checklist and lightweight eval harness (to validate generation quality).

We attached a one-pager for Optimize toolkit packaging and what the profiler session looks like. Marcus — can you confirm if a 10% pilot credit is acceptable commercially?

Best,

Quick technical notes from the infra side — adding detail for the latency matrix you requested.

Pilot profile (what we'll run):
- Model: open-gpt-3b-v1.3 (we recommend a 3B-class model for initial pilot to keep inference fast while representing your production load).
- Sequence lengths: 64 / 256 / 512 (we'll run representative prompts from your RFP).
- Batch sizes: 1 / 4 / 8.
- KV-cache: enabled for chat-like sessions (prefix caching of user messages + system prompt).

Expected outcomes (ballpark):
- KV-cache ON: p50 latency ~ 12–22 ms per token (depending on seq length & batch), p95 ~ 28–60 ms. Tokens/sec scales with batch; batch=8 can get 2.0–3.5k tokens/sec on a single A100-class serving pod.
- KV-cache OFF: p50 latency ~ 45–85 ms per token, p95 could spike 120–240 ms for long seqs.

Cost/quality tradeoffs:
- Int8 quantization (post-training static or PTQ with per-layer calibration) typically reduces throughput cost by 15–25% and memory footprint ~30–40% with minimal quality regression on chat prompts when paired with our prefix caching.
- Mixed int8/16 for attention heads is a conservative middle ground if you want lower risk — expect ~10–15% cost saving and near-zero quality regressions.

Deliverables we can attach to the commercial doc (we'll produce the CSV-style matrix): kv_cache_latency_matrix.csv (rows: seq_len, batch, kv_on/off, p50, p95, tokens/sec).

Quick ask: will StratusAI accept Option B (6-week reserved slot) with a 10% pilot-credit concession? That makes the operational plan simpler on our side (we can reserve capacity and run scheduled profilers).

Thanks,
